rationale: The Codex and OpenCode CLIs are credential-bearing tools that each operator
authenticates individually, and they publish new versions on their own
cadence. Pinning a SHA-256 for them here would tie an infra-cod release to a
vendor build that is usually stale by the time the release is installed, and
would make a routine agent update a full reinstall.
Nothing in this repository installs them today. The runtime supervisor only
execs `codex` and `opencode` from a fixed PATH (/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin),
so on a host where they are absent the panel comes up and the first agent
task fails with ENOENT. Provisioning them is Stage 11 onboarding work.
Until then the contract is: the operator installs them onto the runtime PATH,
and `infra-cod doctor` reports runtime.agent_cli.codex / .opencode as a
warning naming exactly that, so an installation never looks complete when an
What the installer does guarantee is everything a workspace needs before an

packageNotes.git: Required at runtime: every project workspace is cloned with it. Installed by install.sh and checked by `infra-cod doctor`.
packageNotes.postgresql-17: Installed from PGDG, which install.sh configures first — neither postgresql-17 nor postgresql-client-17 exists in Ubuntu 24.04's own archive.
packageNotes.minisign: Needed by the pre-install gate to verify the release signature before anything is written to /opt.
